Originally posted by mr.jenkins:
I am cancelling my Dota Plus subscription and will no longer spend money on Dota 2 events until the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system is fixed.

I also want to get a refund for the rest of already paid 1-year dota plus subscription.

The problems have already been extensively documented in Valve's official GitHub repository:

- https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/issues/35226
- https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/issues/33850
- https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/issues/34303
- https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay/issues/35163

I see no reason to continue financially supporting a game while these issues remain unresolved.

Dota 2's Behavior and Communication System Needs a Serious Rework
17 Oct @ 6:54am
Hiroshi
My solution is very simple, strict and effective:

In my opinion not all players should be able to report, because the system as it is right now is abusive.

You should be able to report someone only if you had a streak of games that earned you a report.
I'd rather see the system put more weight on whether someone's reports are consistently accurate, instead of treating the number of reports as enough reason to punish someone.

Dota 2's Behavior and Communication System Needs a Serious Rework
17 Oct @ 9:43pm
Hiroshi
And if you react badly after being trolled for 40 minutes, you might end up getting reported yourself.

I'm not saying your reaction was necessarily the right one, but the system should be able to distinguish between someone deliberately ruining a game and someone reacting to a teammate who's doing it.
The frustrating part is that even if you decide not to care anymore, the system can still punish you for how you react to someone deliberately ruining the match. That's why I think the system needs to distinguish between the two.
